mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has rebounded from -35.7% to -21.4% over three weeks, signaling outdoor activity resumption. This behavioral shift toward non-retail recreation reduces substitution pressure on retail-and-recreation venues, causing RETAIL_REC to stabilize or decline further as consumers satisfy recreation demand outdoors rather than indoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 14.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility shows high volatility (-32.3% to -21.1%) with a net 11.2-point recovery, indicating inconsistent return-to-office patterns. This uncertainty suppresses consumer confidence and discretionary spending, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed as workers delay non-essential shopping trips pending clearer workplace reopening signals.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES volatility range is 11.2 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined monotonically from -59.1% to -51.0%, indicating persistent public-transport avoidance. Low transit usage constrains retail accessibility for non-car-dependent populations, suppressing RETAIL_REC footfall. If TRANSIT continues declining or stagnates below -50%, retail recovery will be structurally limited.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -51.0% in t-0w, highest in four weeks but still severely depressed
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 10 percentage points over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -1.7% (nearly baseline), indicating essential-goods access is normalized. Concurrent RETAIL_REC decline from -33% to -22.7% reflects policy-driven capacity restrictions on non-essential retail, not supply-side constraints. If restrictions remain in place, RETAIL_REC will not recover despite normalized grocery access.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±2% of baseline while RETAIL_REC remains below -20%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM near-baseline stability contrasts with RETAIL_REC depression
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 12 percentage points over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline and policy restrictions are not lifted.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +15.9% to +11.4% over four weeks, indicating gradual return to normal out-of-home activity. This sustained decline in residential excess signals growing consumer mobility and willingness to visit retail venues. RETAIL_REC will recover as residential normalization continues, driven by behavioral confidence restoration.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below +10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.5 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues declining below +10%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility show correlated recovery (WORKPLACES +11.2 points, TRANSIT +8.1 points over four weeks). This joint improvement signals commuting resumption and workplace reopening. Retail recovery depends on whether this commuting recovery translates to weekday retail footfall; if commuters bypass retail for direct home-to-work transit, RETAIL_REC will not recover despite workplace mobility gains.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by more than 5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both series show net improvement over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvements exceeding 5 points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-June timing (t-0w = 2020-06-15) coincides with early summer season. PARKS mobility rebound (-21.4% from -35.7%) reflects seasonal outdoor-activity preference. If this seasonal shift persists, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as consumers substitute indoor retail with outdoor recreation, creating a seasonal headwind lasting through summer.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -25% for three consecutive weeks during June-August
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above -25%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 10.3 points over four weeks (-33% to -22.7%), showing consistent week-on-week gains. This monotonic recovery trend, absent external shocks, will continue as consumer confidence and retail access normalize. The trend itself is the primary driver; RETAIL_REC will improve further over the next four weeks as the recovery trajectory persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 10.3 points from t-3w to t-0w with no reversals
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases by more than 5 percentage points in any single week over the next 28 days, or the four-week mean is lower than the prior four-week mean.
